summary: A Yes vote authorizes Dixon Unified School District to issue $49,000,000 in bonds, repaid by a property tax of about $30 per $100,000 of assessed value, to repair and upgrade classrooms, labs and school facilities.

tax.text: A Yes vote authorizes a $49 million school bond funded by a property-tax levy for facility repairs and upgrades.
tax.quote: Shall Dixon Unified School District’s measure authorizing $49,000,000 in bonds at legal rates be adopted, levying approximately $30 per $100,000 assessed value ($3,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with citizen oversight, independent audits, and all money locally controlled?

schools.text: A Yes vote funds Dixon Unified School District facilities and technology improvements across its seven campuses.
schools.quote: A “YES” vote approves funding for the District’s facilities plan; a “NO” vote rejects the plan.

tax.text: The No campaign opposes the proposed $49 million bond and argues that the district should perform routine upkeep rather than repeatedly seek new bond funding.
tax.quote: Instead of routine upkeep, the District repeatedly returns to voters with large bond measures to fix problems that should never have been allowed to deteriorate this far.
